source.title: Some limitations of norm based generalization bounds in deep neural networks
source.authors: K. Pitas; Andreas Loukas; Michael A. Davies; P. Vandergheynst

record.file_problem: The supplied text is the full paper and appendix. Its title differs from the metadata title: the text is titled “The role of invariance in spectral complexity-based generalization bounds.”
record.tranche_reason: The paper reports that spectral complexity can assign the same value to networks with different generalization errors when image data differ in translation or deformation structure, and argues that the bounds miss relevant invariances.
record.gate_note: The paper also compares theoretical bounds for convolutional and locally connected networks and reports synthetic noise-norm estimates. Those results do not measure a claim version’s named test-error behavior, so they are not rows. Prior-work results cited in the paper are not recorded.
record.test_reason: The study tests spectral-complexity measures, which none of V1–V8 names. It does not measure magnitude-aware sharpness (V7), compare CNN and fully connected test errors (V3), or independently test the random-label result cited as motivation (V1). Its criticism therefore does not qualify as T5 for these versions.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors conclude that the tested spectral-complexity measures miss generalization differences associated with CNN invariances, and derive convolutional and locally connected bounds identical up to logarithmic factors. They advocate incorporating invariances into future analyses; they do not empirically establish equal generalization for those architectures.
record.recipe_differences: The paper evaluates spectral-complexity measures against generalization error across datasets with differing image transformations; it does not reproduce the original random-label memorization experiments or the magnitude-aware sharpness measure in V7.
record.method_sensitivity: The measured GE at a given spectral-complexity value changes with dataset transformation and augmentation percentage; translation augmentation yields better GE than elastic-deformation augmentation at the same metric values.

fits_no_version.finding: Across CIFAR-10 variants, the same CNN has different GE at matched normalized spectral complexity. Translation and elastic-deformation variants have lower GE than the control; increasing their proportion generally lowers GE at matched complexity. Appendix E reports similar conclusions for the Bartlett metric.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Normalized spectral complexity alone can fail to distinguish generalization outcomes across distributions differing in transformations relevant to CNN invariances.

fits_no_version.finding: The derived spectral-complexity bounds for convolutional and locally connected architectures have the same form up to logarithmic factors, despite their different weight-sharing and invariance properties.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: These spectral-complexity bounds capture local sparsity without capturing the invariance advantage attributed to convolutional weight sharing.

record.peer_reviewed: NeurIPS 2019 Workshop on Machine Learning with Guarantees
record.problems: The empirical comparisons are presented in figures without numeric values in the supplied text. The reported experiments use one CNN architecture and CIFAR-10 variants; uncertainty estimates for these GE comparisons are not stated.
record.rows_left_out: The synthetic 1D perturbation spectral-norm experiment and theoretical convolutional versus locally connected bounds are not rows because they do not report the claim versions’ named test-error outcomes. Cited findings from prior work are excluded.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting, natural-label held-out accuracy, and chance-level held-out accuracy under random labels are cited rather than tested.
No width sweep or test-error comparison beyond the interpolation threshold.

No measured test-error comparison between convolutional and fully connected networks, or tests of sparse local learning or convolutional initialization. Theoretical bounds for locally connected networks do not establish these outcomes.
No batch-size or fixed-epoch recipe comparison.
No dropout comparison, including its interaction with training-set size or augmentation.
No magnitude-aware sharpness measurements, generalization-gap rankings against alternative measures, or restriction to similarly low training loss.
No memorization-based example removal and retraining comparison.

record.verdict_notes: The rows' qualitative spectral-complexity findings are supported by the supplied text. Their states are cannot_determine only with respect to V1–V8, since none measures a listed version. No numeric figure values can be recovered from the supplied text, and no additional version-relevant results require missing entries.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization are not tested.
No test-error comparison of convolutional and fully connected classifiers is reported.
The paper studies spectral complexity and data invariances, not the specified magnitude-aware sharpness measure or its ranking against norm- and margin-based measures.
No memorized-example removal experiment is reported.

rows.subject: deep convolutional neural network (architecture in Equation (5))
rows.operation_detail: Measured generalization error against normalized spectral complexity on the control CIFAR-10 dataset across epochs.

conditions.value: Control CIFAR-10; 10000 training images and 10000 test images sampled randomly

rows.measure: Generalization error at a given spectral-complexity value
rows.value: For the same metric value, the CNN exhibits different GE across the different datasets.
rows.note: The paper describes the comparison in text but gives no numeric GE values in the supplied text.
rows.check: Valid control for the spectral-complexity comparison, but it measures no claim version. The stated value summarizes the cross-dataset comparison rather than a separate control outcome; qualitative differences are reported, but numerical values are unavailable.

rows.subject: deep convolutional neural network (architecture in Equation (5))
rows.operation_detail: Measured generalization error against normalized spectral complexity on translated CIFAR-10 across epochs.

conditions.value: Translated CIFAR-10; 5000 base training and 5000 base test images, each set augmented with 5000 random translations

rows.measure: Generalization error at a given spectral-complexity value
rows.baseline: Control CIFAR-10 dataset at the same spectral-complexity value; numeric baseline not stated
rows.value: The network obtains lower GE than on the control dataset at the same metric values.
rows.note: The text says the CNN is more robust to translations than to elastic deformations; no numeric GE values are stated.
rows.check: Lower GE at matched spectral complexity is explicitly reported, but this does not measure any listed version. Spectral complexity is not V7's magnitude-aware sharpness.
